No, I'm not a believer in anything. I prefer and act on things based on my knowledge and if I have proof of something better, I readjust rather than stick with beliefs.

So you don't believe in the theory of evolution? Or Relativity? I personally believe in things that there is evidence for, just as I may believe something that I haven't yet confirmed could be true until my hypothesis has been put to the test, then, based on new information, I believe in the model that best suits that data. Belief is not Faith and even faith itself is not a bad thing if you understand that what you choose to have faith in may not be real.

To clarify, I use the word "belief" as-in "fixed, absolute belief", which should be pretty clear from the given context. I don't think your pedantry is very productive in cases like this.

Rather than believing in things, this is how it works for me: It's about being conscious of the (variable; knowledge-based) odds of different alternatives and picking the strongest one for the situation. For instance, the odds of something like a religious creation story against a scientific explanation are low enough to not pracically be considered at all; there's probably an almost infinite amount things with higher odds than that.

Opposing anything. I don't mind just about any spiritual, political or social views as long as they don't lead to people putting up walls that shield them from new ideas. If I can learn from how you see the world and you can learn from how I see it, then that would be the perfect relationship. There is no need to oppose each other when neither of us is really right or wrong. I don't know if you could, other than theoretically, separate the 3 elements from each other.... There's a level of symbiosis among them, that they influence, and are influenced by, each other.

But on a theoretical level I'd say religious views would be the killer for me, though political views are fairly intrinsic to who I am... But I could agree to disagree on a political stance, distance myself from an issue if it's a flash point, and don't follow party politics that closely as A. I'm not a citizen of the country I live in and so have no vote and B. don't really see a clear difference between one political party or another (even though I do have a general preference for liberal political attitudes)... I tend to distrust politicians no matter what color tie they're wearing.

But as an atheist it's hard for me to maintain a close relationship with someone who has a religious belief that I find unrealistic. It's like inviting cognitive dissonance, knowingly, upon myself. I've been there before... With a JW and also with someone who followed, and believed in the teachings of, TM to the point where it was indistinguishable from a religious belief. While a harmonious day to day life was perfectly possible, there were moments when our beliefs clashed on such a fundamental level that wedges were driven between us. You could argue that a stronger love for each other might be able to overcome those hurdles, but I don't think I'm wired that way and can't live with that kind of internal conflict.

Cultural beliefs aren't really a problem for me (a foreigner, anyway) unless, I guess, you're specifically targeting the more extreme end of the spectrum where prejudices reside. I couldn't get over racism or homophobia, but, in my experience, as I started out saying, those are usually entwined in religious and political beliefs also.
